newsitem.title: MEXICO: Brazil soybeans reported bound for Mexico - USB/ASA.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybeans reported bound for Mexico - USB/ASA.

text.p: Mexican offices of the United Soybean Board and the American Soybean Association USB/ASA said Tuesday there were unconfirmed reports of several vessels of Brazilian soybeans en route to Mexico.

In an update the USB/ASA said if the reports panned out it would mean the shipments would unload in Mexico just before the seasonal tariff goes into effect for soybeans from non-North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) nations.
"If Brazilian beans come into Mexico, there will be pressure on (domestic) prices, the USB/ASA said. It gave no indication of quantities being shipped.

"During the last two weeks, 'several' vessels of Brazilian beans were brought into the United States by Cargill...the market reacted as expected, bringing the price down. FOB mid-bridge prices in Laredo (Texas-Mexico border) were down to $331.00/tonne last week," the USB/ASA added.
FOB mid-bridge Laredo prices for soybeans started to move up from levels around $312.50/tonne February 28 to peak at $345.00 April 30.
Prices then zigzagged to $330.00 (May 15) and $340.00 (May 31) and down to $331.00 on June 13, the USB/ASA reported.
Mexico imposes from August 1, running throughout the winter, a tariff of 15 percent on soybeans imported from non-NAFTA nations. NAFTA nations are the United States, Canada and Mexico.
One major oil crusher confirmed in May that it had sourced two shipments of soybeans from South America, that were quoted at $7 per tonne less than U.S. soybeans at the time.
